problems.problem: The log records Uday as having chosen all three motivation kinds and as having 'Accepted' the composed motivation line and purpose sentence before either was shown to him. The motivation line includes the agent's '(both; strike one if wrong)'. This makes G4 fail.
problems.cause: The agent called k.confirm_states(by='Uday') and k.propose(accepted_by='Uday') instead of k.certify_line(element, draft=...). The kit's propose() does not check that the wording was ever shown, so the prompt rule 'record acceptance only of wording a member has seen' is not enforced.
problems.fix: Kit: propose() should refuse unless decision == session.last_shown[element] from an earlier reply, and confirm_states() should require refers_to=<the answer record that names the states>. Prompt 2b/2d: add 'After the 2b reply, never call k.propose or k.confirm_states for wording or states the member has not seen or named; show composed wording only with k.certify_line(<element>, draft=<wording>), and let the certification record it.'

problems.problem: Each source got one combined review search whose third block is (focus terms) OR (people without diabetes), shown in the table as two separate blocks. The topic's Asian population was in no search, and the card did not say so; it was stated only when the persona asked at msg 22. As a result the claim 'none names an Asian population' rests on a search that never looked for Asian populations.
problems.cause: Prompt Step 3 says 'search for existing reviews of the topic and of the agreed focus' but does not require separate topic and focus searches or a left-out row on run cards. The kit's run_strategy renders OR-joined blocks as ANDed rows; prepare_strategy has a 'Left out on purpose' row, but run cards do not.
problems.fix: Prompt Step 3: 'Run two searches per source and show both: (a) the topic, with every topic concept joined by AND, population included; (b) the focus, the intervention AND the focus terms. Never join a focus block and a topic block with OR. On every card, add a "Left out on purpose" row naming any topic concept not searched and why.' Kit run_strategy: render OR-grouped blocks as one row ('3 or 4: a record needs only one') and add the left-out row.

problems.problem: Your turn holds two requests (does this change your focus; run PROSPERO and send the results). The persona would answer only the first and skip the PROSPERO chore, so M2 fails for these two turns.
problems.cause: Prompt reply-shape item 6 requires the PROSPERO search 'at that step as a numbered item', while Step 3 says 'ask, one question per reply'. Together they force two requests in one turn.
problems.fix: Prompt item 6: replace with 'A search that a step depends on (for example PROSPERO for Step 3) is asked for as its own request, in the reply after the open question is answered; never in the same Your turn as another question.'

problems.problem: The plan map was not shown when Individual Motivation was certified, which the rubric's M1 counts as a missed map event.
problems.cause: The prompt's plan-map triggers (topic recorded, step completed or reopened, session start and end, on request) leave out 'a decision is certified', which rubric M1 requires.
problems.fix: Prompt Plan map: add 'when a decision is certified'. To limit length, the kit's k.certify md should append the compact k.steps_line(), with the full map only on step change. Alternatively, drop certification from the M1 event list so the rubric and prompt agree.

problems.problem: After the bare 'Certify', the reply explained the rule and showed the full CERTIFY line with 'reason: ___' again. Persona moment 6 expects only the reason question, and the self-report says the line 'looks like I might have to retype it'.
problems.cause: Two prompt rules conflict: 'Whenever Your turn asks for a certification, show the line just above Your turn ... even if you showed it before' and 'ask only: "What is your reason, in a few words?"'.
problems.fix: Prompt Certifying: add 'Exception: the reply that asks for a missing reason contains only the status line, a one-line Done ("Recorded your certify; it needs your reason") and Your turn: "What is your reason, in a few words?" Do not show the line again and do not explain the rule.'

problems.problem: The first results table has no 'Says' column quoting each review's checked passage; it shows code-matched terms instead. It also mixes 4 broader rows into the same table, and the selection rule and coverage table are shown up front. The persona 'can't tell which of the reviews matters most for my fat versus muscle question'.
problems.cause: The prompt contradicts itself: Step 3 asks for a second broader table and 'say which rule chose them', while the reply shape says 'Broader results, selection rules ... wait behind "show"'. The kit's first-pass need_A table omits focus_passage, though the protocol table at msg 26 includes it.
problems.fix: Kit search_report for need_A: always render a 'Says' column from focus_passage (about 15 words), and give broader reviews only as a count line ('13 broader reviews: say "show broader"'). Prompt Step 3: replace 'list broader reviews ... in a second short table' with 'give their count and offer "show broader"'; state the rule in one clause of the FACT line.

problems.problem: Msg 26 runs two protocol variants, repeats the full 4-block string twice, and repeats block rows 1-4 with the counts already shown at msg 20. Search 1 (0 records) is a strict subset of Search 2. Full 12-row plan maps appear in three consecutive replies (24, 26, 28). Self-reports at msgs 21, 23 and 27 say the replies are 'very long ... tables I will not read'.
problems.cause: The kit runs both protocol variants. The prompt requires the full card for every variant and full maps at each trigger, with no compact form for repeats.
problems.fix: Kit: run one protocol search (review filter OR review words) AND protocol[ti]. For a variant card, show the exact string, but give rows only for added blocks ('blocks 1-4 as in the review search, counts unchanged [1]-[4]'). Prompt Plan map: 'If the full map was shown in the previous two replies, show only the rows that changed.'

problems.problem: The certified Individual Motivation decision permanently contains the editing instruction '(both; strike one if wrong)'. The learning choice was never resolved, and the record now holds an instruction instead of a decision.
problems.cause: Prompt 2b says 'put both kinds on the certification line marked "(both; strike one if wrong)"', with no rule to remove the marker when the line is certified.
problems.fix: Prompt 2b: 'Put both kinds in the decision, and write outside the line: "Both kinds of learning are included; strike one if wrong." Never put instructions inside a CERTIFY line.' Kit certify_line/certify: refuse a decision containing 'strike one if wrong'.

problems.problem: After moving ahead early, the msg 20 Next line ('I'll ask if these change your focus') contradicts Your turn (certify the purpose); the persona was unsure which comes first. The 'Step 2 ... (Step 3 started early)' status line left them unsure which step they were on, and the purpose line repeated in four consecutive replies 'feels like nagging'.
problems.cause: The prompt's Moving ahead rule moves questions from the early step under Next but does not say that Next must name the blocking item first or why it blocks.
problems.fix: Prompt Moving ahead: 'Next then begins "Once you approve <item>, I will ..."; Your turn says in one clause why the item blocks ("Step 3 cannot finish until the purpose is approved").' Kit k.early: emit that Next text.

problems.problem: Small display errors. Msg 8 says 'Waiting on you: 1' while asking for a name, three numbered answers and consent. Msg 26 describes protocol[ti] as 'title/abstract words'; it searches titles only.
problems.cause: The kit's status_line counts one logged question (L000010) rather than its numbered items, and the kit's block description maps [ti] to the [tiab] wording.
problems.fix: Kit status_line: count the numbered items in a blocking ask. Kit block description: map [ti] to 'words in the title' and [tiab] to 'title/abstract words'.

judge.strengths: Focus capture was clean. The two probes at msg 10 turned 'all of it' into a focus in the persona's own sense; 'Added by me: nothing' was true; the narrowing was reconciled against the whole topic, and the focus was labeled on every search block. Certification integrity held in the chat: the bare 'Certify' was not accepted, reasons were kept as given, certified wordings matched what was shown, and the Certified count was never overstated. Every literature number traces to saved responses and code; I recomputed 6/128, 12 muscle-naming reviews, 137 to 128, the search-end dates and all block counts from the files. The agent sent nothing to a file and packaged the workspace only at the pause. Plain language was close to perfect: no element codes, and log ids only on Sources lines. The first literature FACT came by planning turn 8. The persona's 'what was the search strategy?' got a compact plain answer that explained the OR join and the Asian-population omission. The PROSPERO card states what it leaves out and why.
